items.title: One taxonomy for everything: areas say where, kinds say what
items.brief: Every item gets two independent labels: an area for which part of life, a kind for what shape of thing. Nothing sits in two places.

decision.label: four areas, three kinds
decision.detail: Studies, Projects, Careers, Personal; kinds are repo, course, application

decision.label: two kinds means two things
decision.detail: B3 is a course; 3YP is the repo doing its work

decision.label: one shared taxonomy
decision.detail: In the shared root, served to every app by one HTTP service

decision.label: Project window shows repos
decision.detail: It only resolves a tmux session to a repo, no special cases

alternatives.label: project as anything viewable
alternatives.detail: An application opened in the Project window and showed blank

alternatives.label: a kind called project
alternatives.detail: Meant both area and kind, so 3YP seemed in three places

alternatives.label: deadline as a kind
alternatives.detail: A due date is an attribute of whatever it belongs to

alternatives.label: labelling by storing app
alternatives.detail: Storage is a detail and plays no part in labelling

assumes.label: one area per item
assumes.detail: If two are often needed, areas become tags

assumes.label: tracks belong in Studies
assumes.detail: If Careers prep plans make them misfiled, tracks inherit their goal's area

consequences.label: kairos task types change
consequences.detail: Sheet, coursework, admin, chore; deadlines become due dates on their owner

consequences.label: new screens
consequences.detail: An Application screen now, a course view with Canvas later

consequences.label: shared contract changes
consequences.detail: A repo links to its course; Project view gains questions and due list

consequences.label: Home by area
consequences.detail: One section per area; personal projects go under Projects

context.label: blank application view
context.detail: The first fixtures opened an application in the Project window, blank

context.label: 3YP in three places
context.detail: A kind called project made it seem to belong everywhere

context.label: every case laid out
context.detail: Each area by kind checked with real examples: B15 sheet 3, 3YP, Jump, Futsal

you.text: Do applications and my CV really count as projects ... they are internship applications and my CV, they do not feel like projects
Need to sort how we treat this properly once and for all, as this is a slightly messy taxonomy issue that I would like to sort as it is key for the backend logic
3YP seems to belong in both studies and project, (and course) ... this still feels really clunky ... include, with examples EVERYTHING and where it gets labelled
A studies section could be good actually ... the projects section on the home page could be personal projects, and then 3YP could go in the studies section

items.title: The data directory is data/, not vault/
items.brief: Rename vault/ to data/ and migrate every stored path with it. Stored paths are identity, so a bare rename would duplicate every edited note.

decision.label: one migration, no symlink
decision.detail: Migration 0037 rewrites the stored paths; no compatibility symlink

decision.label: no Obsidian confusion
decision.detail: vault/ read as an Obsidian vault

decision.label: data/ is accurate
decision.detail: It holds notes, backups and caches too, not just the library

alternatives.label: keep vault/
alternatives.detail: Reads as an Obsidian vault, and one sits inside it

alternatives.label: library/
alternatives.detail: The plan's library is the frozen engine; this folder holds more

alternatives.label: rename without migrating
alternatives.detail: Every edited note would silently arrive as a second document

assumes.label: the directory stays one thing
assumes.detail: If it splits into library store and your notes, name the parts then

consequences.label: old MCP sessions break
consequences.detail: Sessions started before the deploy cannot open the database until restarted

consequences.label: prompts keep "vault"
consequences.detail: Model prompts say "knowledge vault" so pass caches stay valid

consequences.label: corpus text unchanged
consequences.detail: Documents mentioning vault/ still do; derived layers never edit them

consequences.label: config, code and deploy change
consequences.detail: Config, code, tests, units, outbox job, server deploy, every stored path

context.label: a misleading name
context.detail: Holds database, notes, caches and backups but reads as an Obsidian vault

context.label: paths are identity
context.detail: Stored paths identify documents, so renaming is not just a rename

context.label: trialled on a copy
context.detail: 1,549 rows across 14 columns rewritten on a server copy first

you.text: the vault should instead be called library or something better as I do not want it being confused with obsidian's vault
data/, and do not worry at all about any running MCP sessions
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, choosing between library/ and data/

items.title: The shared Rust crates live in the locus repository
items.brief: Fold the shared Rust crates into one workspace here. A theme or contract change in design rounds is then one commit, not three steps.

decision.label: four crates, one workspace
decision.detail: eco-dates, locus-theme, locus-contract, locus-tui at this repository's root

decision.label: kairos and keryx keep pins
decision.detail: They repoint here when next touched; the archived old repository still resolves

decision.label: the plan's merge, now
decision.detail: The plan merges once the shared root has real contents; it has them

alternatives.label: separate repo, relative path
alternatives.detail: Builds only with both repositories checked out side by side

alternatives.label: separate repo, git pin
alternatives.detail: Each theme change is a commit and push there, a pin bump here

alternatives.label: git submodule
alternatives.detail: Two commits per change; a forgotten pin builds old code looking current

alternatives.label: the name eco
alternatives.detail: Did not say what the crates are

assumes.label: a shared cadence
assumes.detail: kairos and keryx need crate changes about as often as locus

assumes.label: Python never blocks them
assumes.detail: If it gets in the way of their builds, the crates move to their own repository

consequences.label: a bigger fetch
consequences.detail: kairos and keryx builds fetch this whole repository for two small crates

consequences.label: pins still gate changes
consequences.detail: A crate change reaches kairos or keryx only on a pin bump

consequences.label: one commit per change
consequences.detail: Screen contracts and theme change in one commit during design rounds

context.label: relative-path builds
context.detail: The crates built only with both repositories checked out

context.label: three steps per change
context.detail: Each theme change cost a commit and push there, a pin bump here

context.label: a small repository
context.detail: 4.3 MB of history, against kairos's own 10 MB

you.text: why are we calling it eco? ... should it not be called something more accurate to what it is
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, which renamed eco to locus-shared

you.text: fold the shared crates into the repo now
you.source: 19 Oct 2026, offered its own repo, a submodule, or folding in

items.title: The drop folder is organised by area
items.brief: Keep the drop folder, organised by area like the notes and the tablet. Nothing labels arrivals yet, so a flat folder files everything uncategorized.

decision.label: four area folders
decision.detail: studies/<course>, projects/<name>, careers/<company or general>, personal; root lets the system decide

decision.label: drops are sources
decision.detail: Never counted as your writing, so a third-party document is not attributed to you

decision.label: the path keeps the folder
decision.detail: The later labeller reads the course or project from it

alternatives.label: five type subfolders
alternatives.detail: Mixed what kind of file it is with what it is for

alternatives.label: one flat folder
alternatives.detail: Chosen first, revised the same day: nothing labels arrivals yet

alternatives.label: no hand drop
alternatives.detail: Some files reach no other path, like a downloaded PDF

assumes.label: the labeller is not ready
assumes.detail: Once it is reliable, the folders can go

assumes.label: library keeps old categories
assumes.detail: Each folder maps to one; if retired, folders map to areas directly

consequences.label: your write-ups flip
consequences.detail: Write-ups in projects/ count as sources, including the two OQTS specs

consequences.label: root drops stay uncategorized
consequences.detail: Until the arrival labeller exists

consequences.label: ingest maps folders
consequences.detail: Each area folder sets a category; personal gets its own

consequences.label: outbox script stays outside
consequences.detail: Out of the repository until transcripts sync in Slice 0

context.label: type folders set category
context.detail: Five subfolders mixed what a file is with what it is for

context.label: the plan labels by area
context.detail: And does not list a hand drop at all

context.label: third-party as your writing
context.detail: A .docx in personal or careers counted as yours

you.text: keep it then, but we no longer need the sub-folders, as the system does that for us

you.source: 19 Oct 2026, told the system cannot label yet
19 Oct 2026, on drops in projects/ counting as sources

items.title: How the build is run
items.brief: Each slice gets a spec you approve, mechanical steps under /goal, design in chat, and a closing report. Your time goes on specs and reports.

decision.label: one session per slice
decision.detail: Specs live in docs/redesign/slices/, approved before building

decision.label: checked /goal steps
decision.detail: The judge reads no files, so each step names a printed check and turn bound

decision.label: spec flags departures
decision.detail: It lists your decisions up front and flags departures from the plan

decision.label: chat for design
decision.detail: Keeps you in every step, which suits design at the screen

alternatives.label: chat for every step
alternatives.detail: Drifts and loses context over a long slice

alternatives.label: plan mode
alternatives.detail: Blocks edits until a written plan is approved

alternatives.label: fan-out workflows
alternatives.detail: Suited to wide jobs, not ordered slices

assumes.label: /goal stays on spec
assumes.detail: If runs drift or stop early, steps become smaller and chat-driven

assumes.label: specs get read
assumes.detail: If you skim them as a chore, specs get shorter

consequences.label: a spec before each slice
consequences.detail: Costs time up front; small slices may get a short one

consequences.label: /goal needs auto mode
consequences.detail: Session-scoped, and runs unattended only in auto mode

consequences.label: Slice 1 in chat
consequences.detail: The design work, done with you at the screen

context.label: your role is planning
context.detail: So which way to execute: /goal, chat messages, or something else?

context.label: checked against the docs
context.detail: Claude Code docs, 19 Oct: the /goal judge sees only the transcript

you.text: the key part of my work is the planning and guidance for the system, I want to make sure we use the best method for executing the plan (ie slash goal or just chat messages to 'start slice 0' etc...)

consequences.detail: A table marks which engine sections are on their way out
